---
type: wordle
title: Subtracting two fractions, a/b − c/d
lhs: "a/b − c/d ="
answer: ( ad − bc ) ÷ bd
keys: ( ) ad bc ac bd + − ÷
---

## Hint
The bottoms $b$ and $d$ are different. Cross multiply to give both fractions the bottom $bd$.

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}
  % a/b - c/d with the two cross products
  \node (a) at (0,0.45) {$a$};
  \node (b) at (0,-0.45) {$b$};
  \draw[seg] (-0.3,0) -- (0.3,0);
  \node (c) at (2,0.45) {$c$};
  \node (d) at (2,-0.45) {$d$};
  \draw[seg] (1.7,0) -- (2.3,0);
  % cross products: a times d, c times b
  \draw[callout, red!65!black] (a) -- (d);
  \draw[callout, blue!65!black] (c) -- (b);
  \node[fill=white, inner sep=1pt] at (1,0) {$-$};   % drawn last so the arrows don't hide it
  \node[red!65!black, font=\footnotesize] at (1,-1.15) {$a \cdot d$};
  \node[blue!65!black, font=\footnotesize] at (1,1.15) {$c \cdot b$};
  \node at (4.3,0) {$= \dfrac{\textcolor{red!65!black}{ad} - \textcolor{blue!65!black}{bc}}{bd}$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

## Hint
Each top is multiplied by the **other** fraction's bottom. Keep the minus sign in the middle, and keep $a$'s product first.

## Solution
**Answer:** $\frac{a}{b} - \frac{c}{d} = \frac{ad - bc}{bd}$

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \frac{a}{b} - \frac{c}{d} &= \frac{a \cdot d}{b \cdot d} - \frac{c \cdot b}{d \cdot b} \\
                              &= \frac{ad - bc}{bd}
\end{aligned}
$$

- **ac** or **bd** on top: that multiplies straight across, which is the rule for *multiplying* fractions, not adding or subtracting them.
- **( bc − ad )**: backwards. That gives the opposite sign.
